paragraphs: Children in care in Norfolk are looked after by Norfolk County Council's own fostering service and by the independent fostering agencies listed on this page. In February 2026 the council said that on average five children a week come into its care, and that it has a network of around 300 fostering households caring for everyone from babies to young adults. It believes many children now living in residential homes could do well in a foster family instead.

In January 2026 the council agreed new investment in its carers. This includes a 15% rise in fees for mainstream and kinship carers, further increases for mainstream carers looking after children aged 10 and over, better rewards for long service, and a larger therapeutic support team, with extra clinicians, specialist training and closer support in a carer's first two years.

Norfolk is one of 11 councils in Foster East, a collaboration of local authorities across the east of England. The council welcomes carers from any background: you do not need to be married or own your home, but you do need to be able to give a child stability, care and encouragement.

Agencies set their own fees and support, so it is worth speaking to the council and two or three of the agencies below, and asking each about training, out-of-hours help and what they pay, before you choose.

sources.title: Norfolk welcomes national focus on fostering (Norfolk County Council, February 2026)
